newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton prices rise on state buying.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton prices rise on state buying.

text.p: Indian cotton prices gained on Friday on increased buying by state-owned agencies as well as higher overseas demand, deales said.
Indian exporters are seeing higher overseas interest after the central government allowed the export of one million bales (170 kg each) during the current cotton season.

In spot deals Bengal-deshi rose by 5/10 rupees to 830/865 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Punjab F-414 gained by five rupees to 1,840/1,860 rupees. Gujarat Sankar-4 (long-staple) rose by 100 rupees to 18,100/18,600 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) for the superior variety.
